directAnswer: Pope Callixtus III was Alfonso de Borja of Xàtiva, the first pope from the Kingdom of Valencia and the first of the Borgia family, who reigned from 8 April 1455 to 6 August 1458. He devoted his pontificate to a crusade against the Ottomans, ordered the retrial that vindicated Joan of Arc, and extended the Feast of the Transfiguration to the whole Church.

sections.h2: Alfonso de Borja, Jurist of Aragon
paras: Alfonso de Borja was born at Xàtiva near Valencia. He studied and taught law at Lleida and entered the service of King Alfonso V of Aragon. He helped bring about the submission of Clement VIII, successor to Benedict XIII's line, in 1429, ending the last remnant of the Western Schism, and was rewarded with the bishopric of Valencia.
Eugene IV made him a cardinal in 1444. When Nicholas V died, the cardinals, divided between the Colonna and Orsini factions, elected Alfonso, then about seventy-six, as a compromise.

sections.h2: The Crusade and the Relief of Belgrade
paras: Two years after the fall of Constantinople, Callixtus made the war against the Ottomans his central concern. He sent preachers across Europe, levied taxes for the crusade and built a papal fleet. In 1456 he ordered church bells to be rung at midday to call the faithful to pray for the defenders of Christendom, a practice linked to the later noonday Angelus bell.

In July 1456 the Hungarian commander John Hunyadi, with crusaders inspired by the Franciscan St. John of Capistrano, broke the Ottoman siege of Belgrade. When news of the victory reached Rome on 6 August, Callixtus extended the Feast of the Transfiguration, kept on that date, to the universal Church, a decree issued in 1457.

sections.h2: The Rehabilitation of Joan of Arc
paras: Joan of Arc had been condemned and burned at Rouen in 1431. At the request of her mother and family, and with the support of the French crown, Callixtus authorized a new inquiry in 1455. On 7 July 1456 the papal commissioners declared the original trial null and void, clearing her name. Joan was canonized much later, in 1920.
In 1455 he also canonized the Dominican preacher St. Vincent Ferrer, a fellow Valencian.

Callixtus brought many Catalans and Valencians to Rome and promoted his relatives. In 1456 he made two nephews cardinals, among them Rodrigo de Borja, who would later become Pope Alexander VI, and he gave another nephew high military command in the Papal States. These appointments caused resentment among the Romans.
He died in Rome on 6 August 1458, the feast he had extended to the whole Church.

keyFacts: Born Alfonso de Borja at Xàtiva; first Valencian pope and first Borgia pope
Former bishop of Valencia and adviser to Alfonso V of Aragon
Ordered midday bells and prayers for the crusade; Belgrade relieved in 1456
Extended the Feast of the Transfiguration (6 August) to the universal Church
Authorized the retrial that annulled Joan of Arc's condemnation (1456)
Made his nephew Rodrigo, the future Alexander VI, a cardinal; died 6 August 1458

faqs.question: How did Callixtus III help Joan of Arc?
faqs.answer: He authorized a new inquiry into her case in 1455. In July 1456 papal commissioners declared her 1431 condemnation null and void.

faqs.question: Why is the Transfiguration celebrated on 6 August?
faqs.answer: The feast was already kept on that date in many places. Callixtus III made it universal after news of the victory at Belgrade reached Rome on 6 August 1456.

faqs.question: Was Callixtus III related to Pope Alexander VI?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rodrigo de Borja, who became Alexander VI in 1492, was his nephew, and Callixtus made him a cardinal in 1456.
